title: Tidy and Reverse a Sentence
statement:
`text` holds words made of lowercase letters, separated by spaces. It may have extra spaces at the start, at the end, and several spaces between words.

Return the words in **reverse order**, joined by **exactly one space**, with no space at the start or the end. If there are no words, return an empty string.
constraints: text contains only lowercase English letters and spaces

examples.explanation: The four words reversed, with single spaces and nothing at the edges.
A single word stays as it is.

hints.nudge: What is a 'word' in terms of the characters? Where does one start and where does it end?
hints.pattern: Scan from the END of the text: skip spaces, then take the word that ends there, and repeat until the start is reached.
hints.pseudocode:
words = empty list; i = last index
while i >= 0:
  skip spaces going left
  if i < 0: stop
  j = i; go left while the character is not a space
  add text[i+1 .. j] to words
return the words joined by one space
hints.walkthrough: Many languages can do this with a built-in split on whitespace, reversing the pieces and joining them; that is the shortest answer. To do it by hand, go through the text from the right: first skip any spaces, then remember where a word ends (j), walk left until a space or the start, and the characters between are one word. Collect the words in the order you meet them: the last word comes first, which is already the reversed order. Join them with a single space; when there are no words the join of an empty list is the empty string. O(n).
